source.title: Transformers converge to invariant algorithmic cores

record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-model core similarity using CCA and correlations between core coordinates, rather than the original studies' methods. It also compares geometric and statistical similarity for independently trained models.
record.gate_note: Included the reported cross-model core-geometry, CCA, and coordinate-correlation results. Behavioral core ablations and generation steering were not included because they report task behavior, not cross-model representation alignment. Similarity results cited from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study uses its own method (ACE cores compared by projector overlap, principal angles, CCA and correlation of 1D core coordinates) to ask whether independently trained models share representations. It does this across seeds in toy transformers and across six pretrained LLMs from four families. It does not use the originals' kernel-alignment or unit-matching procedures.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that independently trained transformers converge on compact, causally necessary and sufficient cores shared across realizations. Markov seeds embed cores in nearly orthogonal subspaces yet are statistically aligned with identical spectra. Modular-addition seeds share cyclic mechanisms with different modes. Six LLMs share a 1D agreement axis that the authors call largely independent of architecture, corpus and scale. They leave open whether this scales to complex tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Algorithmic Core Extraction, causal core validation, CCA, and correlations of one-dimensional core coordinates; it does not reproduce the original studies' measurement procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: For the Markov-chain cores, geometric projector overlap and principal angles indicate near-orthogonality, whereas CCA indicates strong statistical alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Markov-chain models have near-zero cosine similarity between learned weights (~0.03–0.05) despite equal accuracy (Fig. 1A).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently trained networks with equivalent function have dissimilar parameters.

record.peer_reviewed: Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, 2026
record.problems: The language-model comparison concerns one task and its prompt set; the models are not matched for training data or objectives. The study does not relate alignment to measured capability or establish a trend with scale. The seed comparison uses only three toy models, and its geometric and CCA measures give sharply different results. Uncertainty estimates for the reported pairwise correlations are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-bearing representation-similarity results left out. Core ablations and adaptive generation-steering outcomes were excluded because they measure agreement behavior, not cross-model representation alignment.

untested.parts: No capability measure and no explicit test of a trend with scale. Only one task-specific 1D axis is compared, not general representations. No cross-modality comparison.
Entire version: no vision–language or paired image–caption comparison.
No map, stitching, relative representations or unpaired alignment evaluated for loss. The 1D correlations only imply a linear relation of one coordinate.
No neuron-, SAE-feature- or circuit-level comparison. The recurring feature is a single causally validated grammatical-number axis.
No variation of neighbour count, similarity-measure settings, or in- vs out-of-distribution inputs. The measure dependence shown is geometric vs CCA only, in toy models.
No plateau test over scale. No controlled manipulation of shared data or objectives.

missing.what: Operators fit in each seed's Markov core recover the same eigenvalues (0.75±0.25i; 0.48–0.51), matching the true chain. This is functional convergence across seeds.
Each of the six LLMs has a 1D agreement core (spectral gap 40 to 2.8e10), each causally necessary, sufficient and flippable. This is the recurrence of the same feature across models.

record.verdict_notes: The cross-model LLM comparison is a single scalar coordinate per prompt on one task, so it is a narrow test of representational convergence. The V1 scale reading is the reviewer's, from Table A4, not the authors'. The geometric vs CCA contrast compares raw coordinates of separate models, which is expected to differ. Uncertainty is not reported for the correlations. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: The study compares core-coordinate alignment across models of different sizes, but does not test whether alignment rises with size or capability, measure capability as a variable, or test models with different modalities.
No vision-language comparison or paired image-caption representations.
The seed comparison uses three toy Markov-chain transformers and reports core geometry and CCA; it does not compare individual units or establish whether the result generalizes to other tasks.
The study reports similarity measures, but does not test whether a mapping between models preserves behavior with little loss, or test stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
No comparison of recurring interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits.

The study shows dependence on geometric versus statistical similarity measures for toy-model cores. It does not systematically vary the number of neighbours, similarity settings, or input distributions.

The study reports incomplete cross-model correlations and near-orthogonal toy-model cores. It does not test whether shared data or objectives cause the alignment, or whether alignment plateaus over scale.

relationships.condition: Cross-family LLM pairs on subject–verb agreement prompts
relationships.reason: Pairs among the 8B–32B models align at 0.88–0.94, above cross-family pairs involving GPT-2 Small or LLaMA×GPT-2 (0.585–0.79). This is the reviewer's reading of Table A4; the authors do not test a trend (L-S-01, L-P-01, L-S-02, L-P-02, L-S-06, L-P-06, L-S-05, L-P-05, L-S-07, L-P-07, L-S-08, L-P-08, L-S-09, L-P-09).
relationships.display_finding: Pairs among 8B–32B models aligned at 0.88–0.94, compared with 0.585–0.79 for pairs involving GPT-2, without a formal trend test.
